description:
Point landmarks from [TIGER/Line 2024 `POINTLM`](https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2024/POINTLM/): all **1,088,085** features, one file per state (56 state and territory files), each carrying the `state` USPS code its source file was read from.

`feature_type` decodes each row's `mtfcc` the same way landmarks-area does. Measured nationally, most of these points are cul-de-sacs and locality points — address-system landmarks, not places a person would look for on a map — followed by cemeteries, mountain peaks and summits, and airports or airfields.

The PMTiles archive is a single band at full resolution, built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo) `tiles` (not `pyramid` — there is no coarser geography to step up to below this collection, so every zoom draws this collection's own features, thinned to fit the tile-size cap where a zoom is too dense to draw in full). Statistics come from the GeoParquet; this collection has no `*_moe` columns to exclude.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

landmarks-point-tiles.title: Landmarks — Point (PMTiles)
landmarks-point-tiles.description: Vector tiles rendered from the collection's GeoParquet for map display, layer 'landmarks-point'. The collection description states what each zoom band carries.

landmarks-point.title: Landmarks — Point (GeoParquet, national)
landmarks-point.description: GeoParquet with the collection's features and attributes. Every column carries a description in this collection's table:columns.

thumbnail.title: Landmarks — Point rendered with the default style
thumbnail.description: A rendered card of the collection's own data, drawn with the default style.

styles/default.title: Landmark type
styles/default.description: The five most common point-landmark types nationally -- most of them cul-de-sacs and locality points, address-system landmarks rather than places -- each its own color; every other type draws neutral gray. Measured over all 1,088,085 landmarks with a value: Cul-de-sac (668,308), Locality Point (208,547), Cemetery (103,934), Mountain Peak or Summit (63,097), Airport or Airfield (13,146), and 31,053 other types in neutral gray.

source-pointlm.title: TIGER/Line 2024 POINTLM — point landmarks, state directory
source-pointlm.description: 56 state and territory shapefiles (`tl_2024_<FIPS>_pointlm.zip`), this collection's source.

doc-mtfcc.title: 2022 MAF/TIGER Feature Class Code Definitions
doc-mtfcc.description: The code -> name table `feature_type` was decoded from. TIGER2024 has no 2024 edition of this PDF; 2022 is the nearest published vintage, linked from the Bureau's own index at https://www.census.gov/library/reference/code-lists/mt-feature-class-codes.html. The code set is unchanged between the two: every code this build used also appears, worded the same, in the 2021 and 2025 editions.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: `POINTID`, from TIGER's internal address/point ID scheme -- not a census tabulation GEOID.

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: USPS code of the state file this row was read from.

table:columns.name: feature_type
table:columns.description: `mtfcc` decoded through the 2022 MAF/TIGER Feature Class Code list. The two largest categories nationally (measured, 1,088,085 rows total) are Cul-de-sac (668,308) and Locality Point (208,547) -- both address-system landmarks, not places.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Landmark point, WKB-encoded. Written in the source CRS, NAD83 (EPSG:4269) -- unlike the ACS collections, this is kept rather than reprojected to WGS84/OGC:CRS84, so the GeoParquet `geo` metadata carries an explicit `crs` key.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct for the row's geometry (a point's own coordinates, repeated), written by gpio.
